C1.worst_defect: The hero says what it is and who it is for, but nothing on the first screen says whether the hosted till at app.vendurepos.com is free, needs an account, or who runs it, so a buyer comparing it with Square or Shopify POS cannot tell the cost model in five seconds.
C1.where: home/desktop/01 hero ("VendurePOS is an open-source till for Vendure..." and the Live demo / Quick start buttons)

C2.worst_defect: "MIT licensed" and "open-source till" are undercut by "To build and host it yourself ... you need your own RxDB Premium licence token (RXDB_PREMIUM)". The site never says this is a paid third-party licence or what it costs, and nowhere names who is behind the project or app.vendurepos.com (the only hint is analytics going to ph.wcpos.com), so in practice you are tied to an unnamed operator's hosted build.
C2.where: home/desktop/02 'Before you start > Setting up the store' last bullet; connect-a-till/desktop/01 'Where your data goes'; limitations 'Setting up the store'

C3.worst_defect: The path is complete and ends with a real success check. But a known plugin defect is documented in three places instead of fixed: the vendurepos-pos-till role made by 'New POS till key' lacks ReadOrder on 0.3.0, so the till's order history is refused until you edit the role by hand.
C3.where: quick-start 'Optional: a device key for each till'; connect-a-till 'Give each cashier their own account'; changelog 0.2.0 'Not in the release notes'

C4.worst_defect: Troubleshooting warns that clearing site data "deletes this till's unsent sales, refunds and register records", but every other page says that on plugin 0.3.0 the till cannot refund ("On plugin 0.3.0 the till cannot refund"), so the docs contradict themselves about refunds on a real store.
C4.where: troubleshooting 'Act on a header notice > Till updates line' vs at-the-till 'Refund a sale'

C5.worst_defect: The hero product shot is the full desktop till scaled into a 990 px frame, so its cart lines, tax rows and header text render at about 8–9 px and cannot be read. Below it, 'What it does today' switches from two boxed cards to eight unboxed text blocks, which reads as two different designs.
C5.where: home/desktop/01 (hero image and 'What it does today' section)

C6.worst_defect: Code samples wrap mid-statement at 390 px (e.g. "import { generateMigration } from" breaking before '@vendure/core', and generateMigration's options split over three lines), so copy-reading on a phone is awkward. Tables collapse well into labelled cards.

C7.worst_defect: The SoftwareApplication JSON-LD has no softwareVersion (0.3.0) and no offers/price, so search results cannot show that it is free or what version it is. Everything else is clean: Lighthouse 98/100/100/100, llms.txt, sitemap, search API, an og card, and a real 404.

overall_worst.defect: The site sells an 'open-source, MIT licensed' till, but self-hosting needs an RxDB Premium licence the site never says is paid, and the hosted alternative at app.vendurepos.com has no named operator, price or continuity promise. A sceptic advising a client cannot tell whether they are adopting open source or depending on an anonymous hosted service, so I would warn them off.
overall_worst.where: home/desktop/02 'Setting up the store' last bullet; connect-a-till/desktop/01 'Where your data goes'
overall_worst.fix: Add one plain sentence beside the RXDB_PREMIUM note: who runs app.vendurepos.com and that it is free, that RxDB Premium is a paid commercial licence from RxDB (with a link to its pricing), and what happens to tills if the hosted build goes away (it is static files you can host yourself with that licence).
